Lessons.Title: Graphs of Linear Functions
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goals: graph lines by plotting points and using slope/intercepts; infer a line formula from a graph; identify parallel and perpendicular relationships; construct lines through points; solve two-line systems.
To graph f(x)=mx+b, mark (0,b), then move horizontally and vertically according to rise/run. Check a second point for accuracy.
Two distinct nonvertical lines are parallel iff they have equal slope. Perpendicular nonzero slopes multiply to −1. A vertical line x=c is perpendicular to a horizontal y=k.
Find line formulas from two coordinates or from an intercept and slope. A vertical line cannot be expressed as a single-valued y=f(x) over its x-coordinate.
The intersection of two lines has the same x-input and y-output for both equations. Algebraically solve f(x)=g(x) and substitute back.
Independent Edulytics Cool-down: (a) Sketch y=−2x+4 from its intercept and rise/run. (b) Find a perpendicular through (1,2) to y=2x−3. (c) Solve intersection of y=x+1 and y=5−x.
Independent Try It 1 — Graph by coordinates. Plot f(x)=−3x/4+6 using x=0,4,8.
Independent Try It 2 — Find negative-input point. For f(x)=−2x/3+5 find a point with negative x.
Independent Try It 3 — Transform a line. Describe identity transformations producing y=2x+4.
Independent Try It 4 — Find zero. Find x-intercept of y=x/4−4.
Independent Try It 5 — Parallel and perpendicular through origin. Given h(x)=2x−4, find a parallel line through origin and a perpendicular one.
Independent Try It 6 — Perpendicular to two-point line. Line through (−2,−15),(2,−3): find a perpendicular through (6,4).
Independent Try It 7 — Analyze two intersecting models. For j(t)=3t−4, h(t)=5−t: find each intercept, slope signs and intersection.

KeyConcepts.Title: Graphing by points
KeyConcepts.Definition: Substitute 2 or more x-coordinates into a linear function.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Three points provide a useful error check.

KeyConcepts.Title: Slope-intercept graph
KeyConcepts.Definition: Plot b at (0,b) then use slope m as rise/run.
KeyConcepts.Rule: A negative slope lowers y as x increases.

KeyConcepts.Title: Line from graph
KeyConcepts.Definition: Read any two distinct plotted points to find slope, then solve intercept.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Avoid reading noisy grid labels without point confirmation.

KeyConcepts.Title: Special lines
KeyConcepts.Definition: y=k is horizontal and constant; x=k is vertical and not a function y=f(x).

KeyConcepts.Title: Parallel relationships
KeyConcepts.Definition: Distinct nonvertical lines are parallel when their slopes coincide.

KeyConcepts.Title: Equation through point
KeyConcepts.Definition: Use y−y1=m(x−x1) with the required slope.
KeyConcepts.Rule: For a perpendicular slope take negative reciprocal.

KeyConcepts.Title: Linear systems
KeyConcepts.Definition: At intersection the outputs of both functions are equal.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Solve f(x)=g(x) and substitute into one.

KeyConcepts.Title: Break-even
KeyConcepts.Definition: Sales revenue equals total fixed plus variable production cost.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Check units and admissible nonnegative quantities.

Visuals.Title: Same slope, different intercepts
Visuals.Description: Parallel first-party lines share slope but not offset.

Visuals.Title: Intersecting line outputs
Visuals.Description: Two lines meet when their y-output is the same.

SummaryPoints: Plot at least two exact points for each line.
Equal slopes yield parallel lines; negative reciprocal slopes yield perpendicular lines.
Vertical lines are not functions y=f(x).

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Slope m equals output change divided by input change.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Using a rounded plotted intersection as an exact algebraic solution.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Small graph scale errors can change the answer.
